summary: Yellowstone NP lookout: boards between trees by 1934, then a CCC 60-foot wooden pole tower in 1937; listed as gone, with no removal date or site description found.

facts.design: Wooden pole tower about 60 feet (18.3 m), built on the ground and raised into position; the earlier station was boards strung between two trees
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com; no removal date found

access.note: Inside Yellowstone National Park; no source describes the former site or how it can be reached

events.note: First lookout station existed as early as 1934: boards strung between two trees
Second tower erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps; 60-foot tower reported complete in September 1937
Within two hours of completion, the tower was used to spot a fire in nearby Idaho (per 1937 Pinedale Roundup report quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Registered May 22, 2022; nominated by Edward Stark

corrections.proposed: 1937 built (CCC tower); 1934 first station of boards strung between two trees
corrections.why: The FFLOS infobox shows Built 1934, but its description places the 1934 boards-between-trees station and the second tower, erected in 1937, as separate things.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS infobox says 1934, while its description and the 1937 newspaper reports date the tower to 1937. The story dates the tower to 1937 and the first station to 1934.

sources.title: Bechler River R.S. Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: 1937 newspaper wording is read through the Forest Lookouts transcription; original papers were not checked. The Forest Lookouts page has a 'Removed' heading with no text, so removal date is unknown. 'Gone' rests on the FFA and firelookout.com lists. The NPS rephotography finding aid mentions a 1935 Bechler River panorama but does not describe the site, so it was not used. A 1937 photo is captioned on the FFLOS page but no image URL was captured, so no photo entry was added. The access level 'public' reflects Yellowstone National Park land only.
